exposure: delivery body mass index (BMI) 60 or greater
outcome: Composite neonatal morbidity (5-minute Apgar score less than 7, hypoglycemia, respiratory distress syndrome, sepsis, hospital stay greater than 5 days, neonatal intensive care unit admission, or neonatal death)
Maternal complication rates (labor induction, cesarean delivery, wound complication, postpartum hemorrhage, and hospital stay greater than 5 days)
cohort: Singleton pregnancies between 23 and 42 weeks of gestation
finding: BMI 60 or greater at the time of delivery is significantly associated with increased neonatal morbidity and maternal complication rates compared to women with lower BMI.
